interest: This collection provides historians with an invaluable micro-level view of the bureaucratic mechanics, diplomatic tensions, and security procedures that shaped the reopening of occupied Japan to international commerce and travel. The detailed individual dossiers reveal the complex intersections of Allied military control with private enterprise, family reunification, and religious missions, while documenting unexpected economic anxieties ranging from Malayan resentment over British trade quotas to domestic protests against the exit of Japanese chick sexers.
overview: This file documents the diplomatic and administrative mechanisms governing civilian travel, residence, and commercial access to occupied Japan throughout 1947. Coordinated among the Department of State, the War Department, and General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)—primarily under SCAP Circular No. 8 and Circular No. 12—the records capture both high-level policy implementation and detailed individual casework. Key subjects include the management and diplomatic negotiation of national private-trader quotas, security vetting, missionary clearances and logistical support, emerging commercial air transit procedures, port quarantine controls, and repatriation.
